questions.prompt: True or false: “South Africa shares a land border with Mozambique.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Climate” part of the South Africa article.

questions.proof: There is a desert in the southern Namib in the farthest northwest and subtropical climate in the east along the Mozambique border and the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with South Africa?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture South Africa on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Climate” part of the South Africa article.

questions.proof: There is a desert in the southern Namib in the farthest northwest and subtropical climate in the east along the Mozambique border and the Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: What money is used in South Africa?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in South Africa is the rand.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: South Africa about 1,221,037 square kilometres; Tanzania about 947,303 square kilometres; Mozambique about 801,590 square kilometres; Botswana about 581,737 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of South Africa?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Society and culture” part of the South Africa article.

questions.proof: Urban blacks normally speak English or Afrikaans in addition to their native tongue.
